request.description: Returns title, description, duration, totalQuestions, totalMarks, isPublished, isPaid, testSeries, paperType, examDate, attemptsCount for each test.

testSeries is now required — every test must belong to a series (category is derived from testSeries.category, not set directly on Test). sections carries the per-subject exam-pattern breakdown and must have at least one entry. duration is always computed server-side as the sum of every section's duration (any duration sent here is ignored) — do not send it. totalQuestions/totalMarks are left alone here too; they're auto-calculated from actual Question documents as they're added (see Questions (Admin) > Create Question). paperType defaults to "mock" — omit examDate unless paperType is "previous_year" (see the sibling "Create Previous Year Paper" example). attemptsCount is server-managed (incremented on test start) and cannot be set here.

Same endpoint as Create Test — paperType: "previous_year" plus examDate is what distinguishes a previous-year paper from a regular mock test. Everything else (sections, duration, totalQuestions/totalMarks) works exactly the same.
Sending sections recomputes duration as the sum of the new sections. Omitting sections leaves duration untouched.

CSV columns: test, section, questionText, option1, option2, option3, option4, correctAnswer(1-based), marks, explanation, order. section is matched by name against the target test's sections[].name (case-sensitive exact match).
section must be one of the target test's sections[]._id (see Create Test's response, or {{sectionId}} which Create Test captures automatically from its first section).

Resuming an existing in-progress attempt is race-safe — a DB-level partial unique index on (user, test) while status is "in-progress" means two near-simultaneous calls can't create duplicate attempts; the losing request just resumes the winner's attempt (resumed: true) instead of erroring.
404s if questionId doesn't belong to this attempt's test or has since been soft-deleted by an admin (isActive: false) — answers are never accepted against an inactive question.

score/breakdown/unattempted are all scoped to currently-active questions — a question soft-deleted after being answered no longer contributes marks and is excluded from the unattempted count too, so the numbers stay internally consistent.

404s for an inactive or (non-admin-viewed) unpublished test, matching Get Test By Id's convention. Ranks the best attempt per user (highest score, fastest submit as tiebreak) among completed/auto-submitted attempts.

formdata.value: India Approves First Offshore Airport in Maharashtra's Palghar District

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has given in-principle approval for India's first offshore airport, to be built off the coast of Palghar district near Kore Beach, roughly 4.75 km from the Uttan-Virar Sea Link. Proposed by the Maharashtra Airport Development Company (MADC), it will be built on reclaimed land in the Arabian Sea with two runways designed to handle around 90 million passengers annually, becoming the third major airport serving the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Construction is expected to begin in 2026, with operations projected for the early 2030s.
Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis approved India's first offshore airport, to be built near Kore Beach, Palghar — designed for 90 million passengers a year.
